Resolves #19656

The 96 specs the `neuralLink` fixture gates now run in hosted CI, on `dev` pushes only. This is the burn-in epic #19655 asks for before any pull request depends on them.
- `.github/workflows/test-e2e-brain.yml`: one job resolves the Brain's `dev` tip. Six shards then check out the Engine and the Brain at that SHA, install the Brain with its own `npm ci`, set `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`, and run their share of the Brain-gated specs.
- `e2eCiSelection.mjs` gains `--brain-paths` (the selection) and `--brain-receipt` (each shard's job-summary receipt). The selection and its report share one source, as they do for the engine tier.
- `WhiteboxE2E.md` gains the Brain setup step it never had, and a hosted-CI section that says where the receipts are.

Evidence: L2 (a hosted run of this branch through a temporary push trigger, removed before review; a local clean-clone Brain smoke) → L3 required for the `dev`-push receipts. Residual: the first `dev`-push receipts. Residual-Owner: #19655 (the promotion leaf #19657 is blocked by them).

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | The only trigger is `on: push: branches: [dev]`; there is no `pull_request` trigger. The branch entry used for the pre-review run is not in the final diff. |
| AC-2 | The `brain` job runs `git ls-remote https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain refs/heads/dev` once. Every shard checks out `needs.brain.outputs.sha`, and a rerun replays that output. Each receipt records it beside `github.sha`, the event and `run_attempt`. |
| AC-3 | The Brain is prepared by its own `npm ci --foreground-scripts`, whose `prepare` writes its server configs. The workflow sets only `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`, which is the Engine fixture's input, and reads or writes no Brain configuration. ADR-0019 was read before authoring. |
| AC-4 | Each receipt states its test-step time against the five-minute ceiling, marked **over** past it. It also states its population (N of the 96 Brain-gated files, beside the engine tier's 49 Brain-free ones) and its outcome. A shard with no report or an unfinished step says so instead of reporting zero. |
| AC-5 | `WhiteboxE2E.md` § Hosted CI. |

## Deltas from ticket
- **Six shards, 30-minute step bound, 45-minute job bound.** The burn-in measures how long the tier takes, so no bound is set to end it early. The receipts compare against the five-minute ceiling, and the promotion leaf picks the shard count from them.
- **No scope classifier.** Every `dev` push is a sample. The engine tier's impact boundary does not yet cover AI-client or NL fixture changes; extending it is the promotion leaf's job.
- **Concurrency.** A started measurement completes. A newer `dev` head replaces only the run still queued, so the burn-in never holds more than one run's shards.
- **Only Playwright's `ffmpeg` is installed.** The browser is the runner's Chrome channel, which the engine tier already runs on hosted. The first hosted run showed that the video-recording specs still need `ffmpeg-1011`.
- **The Brain installs its own pinned `neo.mjs`**, as a maintainer's checkout does. Its `npm ci` is the whole preparation.

## Test Evidence
- `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/E2eCiSelection.spec.mjs`: 8 passed. The three new arms cover the selection (exactly the fixture-gated specs) and both receipt branches.
- Local clean-clone smoke: the Brain at its `dev` tip `b3cad9f1a8`, provisioned only by its own `npm ci` (8 s, `prepare` wrote the configs), then two Brain-gated specs on a private bridge port: 7 passed in 17 s.
- Two hosted runs of this branch: Brain `dev` tip `b3cad9f1a8`, with the push trigger temporarily widened and then dropped in the last commit.
  - [run 1](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38258413156): 247 passed, 14 failed, 4 skipped. Three of the reds were mine: video-recording specs without `ffmpeg`, fixed in `0b4cbd39a2`.
  - [run 2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38260376912): 251 passed, 10 failed, 4 skipped. Test-step times per shard were 3m43s, 2m08s, 4m17s, 2m09s, 11m39s and 5m33s, so shards 5 and 6 are over the ceiling at six shards.
  - The reds across both runs are the burn-in's first finding, for #19655 and the promotion leaf:
    - **Needs a Memory Core:** `DemoBDockTransactionsNL` and `TransactionArchiveReplay` fail 2/2 with `archive-store-unavailable` (no `NEO_MCP_REMOTE_TOKEN`).
    - **Deterministic on hosted, 2/2:** `DeltaCoherenceRegistryNL` (the grid header button never renders), the `WorkstationDragAffordancesNL` re-entry test, `WorkstationFilmTourNL` ×2 and `WorkstationPopOutSparklinesNL`. All five pass locally at the same Brain (`b3cad9f1a8`) and Engine SHAs: `DeltaCoherenceRegistryNL` 1/1 in 10.9 s, and the three workstation files 10 passed, 1 skipped. They are hosted-environment reds, not `dev` regressions.
    - **Intermittent, 1/2:** `ButtonBaseNL` ×2, `DockSplitterZoneIdNL`, `WorkstationFiveBeatNL`, `WorkstationPopOutHoverSyncNL`, `WorkstationPopOutPaneIdentityNL` and `WorkstationReclaimEmbodimentNL`.
  - This PR records these reds and does not dispose of them. Matching them against #17844's local reds (its 10-08 census: 437 passed, 19 red) is the next cross-check.
- `check-guard-ci-parity` OK, `check-ticket-archaeology` 0, `check-file-sizes` 0 violations.

## Addressed Review Feedback

Responding to Euclid's review (CHANGES_REQUESTED at `7253c7204b`, review 5492645339).

**Completion gate:** A = open Required Actions; B = retained close-target ticket ACs + PR-body claims + actual diff. A is empty relative to B at `15dbe12a5a`.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** **[P2] Restrict the new burn-in workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN permissions to its required read access.** The measured setup grants broad writes, both checkouts persist the credential, and Brain install lifecycle code executes under that job. Declare the least-privilege scope in `.github/workflows/test-e2e-brain.yml`, such as `permissions: contents: read`, preserving checkout/preparation and artifact receipts. The [checkout owner's recommendation](https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/main/README.md#recommended-permissions) is contents read; [GitHub's permission contract](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions) disables unspecified scopes when a scoped declaration is supplied.
      **Commit:** `15dbe12a5a`
      **Details:**
      - The workflow now declares a top-level `permissions: contents: read`, and both checkouts set `persist-credentials: false`. This follows the repository's own `file-size-guard.yml` pattern. The Brain's lifecycle scripts can therefore see neither a write-scoped token nor a stored credential.
      - Nothing the job does needs more scope:
        - the `brain` job runs `git ls-remote` against a public repository without a token;
        - both checkouts are public reads;
        - the receipt writes to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which is a file.
      - Uploading the failure artifacts works under `contents: read`. Three org workflows already do it: neo-stage's `smoke.yml` (its `stage-smoke` upload ran on neo-stage#10 today) and the Brain's `brain-unit.yml` and `brain-integration.yml`.
      - The burn-in can't run on this PR by design. The first `dev`-push run is the live check that checkout, preparation and receipts hold under the narrowed token, and it is already Post-Merge Validation on #19655.

The parsed workflow at this head: `on.push.branches = [dev]`, `permissions = {contents: read}`, and both checkouts carry `persist-credentials: false`. CI is running on `15dbe12a5a`.
